record.context_brief: Sum of entries of an inverse Aztec-diamond Kasteleyn matrix
record.original_question: Let Kn be the Kasteleyn matrix of the Aztec diamond of order n in which every other vertical domino has its sign flipped. Prove that the sum of the entries of K_n^{-1} equals (n-1)(n+3)/2 - 2^(n-1) + 2.

evidence.quote: Consider the Kasteleyn matrix Kn for the Aztec diamond of order n, in which every other vertical domino has its sign flipped (that is, the corresponding 1’s in the bipartite adjacency matrix are replaced by −1’s).
Problem 12: Show that the sum of the entries of the matrix inverse of Kn is (n − 1)(n + 3)/2 − 2^(n−1) + 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 1$. The Aztec diamond of order $n$ is the planar region consisting of all unit lattice squares whose centers $(x+1/2,\, y+1/2)$ satisfy $|x+1/2|+|y+1/2| \le n$. Color these unit squares as a checkerboard, and let $B$ (resp. $W$) be the set of black (resp. white) squares; one has $|B|=|W|=n(n+1)$. Form the bipartite adjacency matrix $A$ indexed by $B \times W$, where $A_{b,w}=1$ if the squares $b \in B$ and $w \in W$ share an edge and $A_{b,w}=0$ otherwise (so each domino in a tiling corresponds to such an edge).

Define the (signed) Kasteleyn matrix $K_n$ to be the matrix obtained from $A$ by flipping the sign of every other vertical edge: more precisely, fix a 2-coloring of the vertical edges of the Aztec diamond into two classes such that any two vertical edges in the same column alternate between the classes (equivalently, vertical edges in even-indexed rows get sign $+1$ and those in odd-indexed rows get sign $-1$); replace the corresponding entries of $A$ by $-1$ for one of the two classes. The matrix $K_n$ is then a square matrix with $\det K_n = \pm \, 2^{n(n+1)/2}$ (the number of domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order $n$).

Prove that
$$\sum_{b \in B,\; w \in W} (K_n^{-1})_{w,b} \;=\; \frac{(n-1)(n+3)}{2} \;-\; 2^{\,n-1} \;+\; 2.$$

artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in James Propp's well-known list of open problems on enumeration of matchings/tilings (the Aztec diamond chapter in MSRI Publications vol. 38). Web search did not return a clear citation announcing a proof of this specific identity for the sum of entries of the inverse Kasteleyn matrix; while inverse Kasteleyn matrices for the Aztec diamond have been computed explicitly (e.g. by Helfgott–Gessel and later authors), no source found verifies this exact closed form has been proven. Status not conclusively established from available sources.

status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to study inverse Kasteleyn matrices for the Aztec diamond, but no explicit confirmation of this identity was located.
